newsitem.title: INDIA: India government likely by Monday - United Front.
newsitem.headline: India government likely by Monday - United Front.

text.p: India's United Front coalition expects to form a new centre-left government with the support of the Congress party before parliament reconvenes on April 21, an alliance spokesman said on Friday.
"The formation of a new government is entirely likely before the parliament resumes on the 21st," coalition spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters in the Indian capital.

The Congress party triggered the current political crisis when it withdrew its support last week from Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 10-month-old administration, and he subsequently lost a vote of confidence in Parliament.
On Friday, Congress leader Sitaram Kesri said in a letter to President Shankar Dayal Sharma that Congress could support a new United Front coalition government -- if Deve Gowda stepped down.
Speaking after a special meeting of the United Front's decision-making steering committee, Reddy said the coalition leaders had seen and accepted the Congress letter of support.

"The standing committee, after reviewing the letter and noting the content, found it quite satisfactory, and therefore decided to go ahead with the process of choosing a new leader for United Front through consensus," Reddy said.

"We hope to complete the process by tonight or (at the) latest by tomorrow," Reddy said, adding that the United Front expected to establish an "institutional mechanism" to coordinate relations with Congress.
Left-wing parties in the United Front had refused to choose a new leader unless Kesri first withdrew a March 31 letter to Sharma staking his claim to form the next government.
That threat helped delay the choice of a new prime minister and raised the prospect of having to call mid-term polls to resolve the impasse.
Neither the United Front nor Congress wants snap elections as opinion surveys show a vote would benefit the right-wing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Kesri moved to break the logjam on Friday with his letter to Sharma offering to back a new United Front government if the alliance replaced Deve Gowda -- but that if they did not, his own March 31 claim to form a government would stand.
Leaders of the 15-party alliance were to meet on Friday night to name a new leader. "The decision can be arrived at tonight or tomorrow morning," Reddy said.
Their choice appeared to have narrowed to G.K. Moopanar, a powerful baron from southern Tamil Nadu state, or Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral, United Front politicians said.
Moopanar, who broke from the Congress last year to form a regional party in Tamil Nadu, has emerged as a frontrunner.
"Moopanar has said he is willing to accept the post," said a senior United Front leader who asked not to be identified.
Gujral's competence and congenial style have endeared him to many but he has a small political base.
